title: A same-level watch replaces silently; a higher-level watch escalates; watches first seen together are evaluated in root issue-time order; watches first seen after an outage
notes: WATA30 serial 900 is synthetic and models a G2 watch superseding a G1 watch.

WATA50 serial 100 and WATA30 serial 901 are synthetic. Both are first seen in step 4: the G3 watch was issued at 17:00 and replaced by the G2 watch at 17:03. The G3 watch is evaluated first, escalates within the new-notice grace, and the G2 replacement is then silent because an earlier watch in the same merge raised a higher rank.

WATA50 serials 101 and 104, WATA30 serials 902 and 905 and WATA20 serial 903 are synthetic. They model watches first seen after alerts outages. In step 9, the G2 and G1 watches issued during the first outage were each superseded before the fetch that first saw them. Each is compared with the watch it replaced, so both are silent and both ranks are recorded. In step 13, the G3 watch issued during the second outage is higher than the G1 watch it replaced, but it ended outside the new-notice grace before it was first seen. It raises nothing and has no rank recorded, so the G2 watch that replaced it raises 'new'.
